description: Gadolinium is a silvery-white, malleable and ductile rare-earth element with atomic number 64. It is the eighth member of the lanthanide series and crystallizes in a hexagonal close-packed structure at room temperature. Below 20°C it is ferromagnetic, and above this temperature it is the most paramagnetic element.
uses: Gadolinium is used as a contrast agent for MRI scans, in nuclear reactors as a neutron absorber and burnable poison, in alloys to improve workability and resistance to oxidation at high temperatures, as a phosphor in medical imaging, as a gamma ray emitter, in electronic and optical devices, and in superconductors. It is also used in neutron radiography and neutron capture therapy.
characteristics: Gadolinium reacts slowly with atmospheric oxygen or moisture to form a black oxide coating, and tarnishes quickly in moist air. It is a strong reducing agent and quite electropositive, reacting slowly with cold water and quickly with hot water. The isotope gadolinium-157 has the highest thermal-neutron capture cross-section among any stable nuclide at about 259,000 barns, and gadolinium demonstrates a magnetocaloric effect where its temperature increases when entering a magnetic field and decreases when leaving one.
